statements.t: The Company expects some of these dynamics to continue for the remainder of 2026, which could continue to have an impact on demand, material costs and labor.

If that happens, we will be required to pay interest at the Base Rate, which is the sum of the higher of (i) the Prime Rate (as publicly announced by the Agent from time to time), (ii) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.50% and (iii) Adjusted Term SOFR for a one-month tenor in effect on such day plus 1.00%.
Our future success will be highly dependent on our ability to access outside sources of capital.
We will continue to have access to the availability currently provided under the Credit Agreement as long as we remain compliant with the financial covenants.
Based on our estimates at this time, we expect to be in compliance with these financial covenants through 2026 and the foreseeable future.
However, future cash flows are subject to a number of variables, and additional capital expenditures will be required to conduct our operations.

In the event we make one or more acquisitions and the amount of capital required is greater than the amount we have available for acquisitions at that time, we could be required to reduce the expected level of capital expenditures and/or seek additional capital.
We cannot guarantee that this additional capital will be available on acceptable terms or at all.

“Our third quarter results were in line with our expectations and reflected strong demand as project volumes continued to accelerate within our Datacenter & Critical Power end market,” said Jag Reddy, President and Chief Executive Officer.
As volumes ramped, Adjusted EBITDA margin improved on a sequential basis through better capacity utilization, while we continued to absorb project launch costs consistent with our expectations.
“During the quarter, we secured approximately $45 million of new Datacenter & Critical Power project awards, and our qualified opportunity pipeline now exceeds $200 million,” Reddy continued.

“Importantly, this demand we are seeing today reflects datacenter infrastructure investments initiated approximately three years ago, as the products we manufacture are typically installed during the later stages of a project build.
Based on our awarded programs and pipeline, we are anticipating reaching full capacity within the next 18 months and have started deploying capital towards expanding our footprint.

On October 1, 2026 we closed on the acquisition of our Thomson, Georgia facility, which, together with planned equipment investment, is expected to add approximately $50 million of annual revenue capacity by 2028 and increase our total revenue capacity beyond the approximately $850 million previously disclosed.”
“We will continue to incur launch costs and deploy capital in a disciplined manner as we position MEC to serve this growing customer base.

While these investments and the ongoing alignment of our operations with customer timelines will remain a factor over the coming quarters, we expect to realize improved operating leverage as volumes continue to ramp.
Today, the Company is updating its financial guidance for the full-year 2026.

The Company’s full-year 2026 guidance assumes a full year of Accu-Fab ownership, incremental Datacenter & Critical Power cross-selling revenue, and continued improvement in Commercial Vehicle and Construction & Access, partially offset by ongoing softness in our Agriculture and Powersports end markets.
